$comment: PURPOSE AND SHAPE: identity and short enumerable facets stay in frontmatter so Bases can tabulate them and Tier 2 can project them; every long-form SCF prose column moves into the Markdown body. Properties: title (SCF Control name), scf_id (SCF #), domain (SCF Domain, 33 values), pptdf_applicability (6 values), csf_function (NIST CSF 2.0 function grouping, 6 values), validation_cadence (3 values), and control_weighting. control_weighting is emitted through the number filter so Bases sorts materiality numerically instead of lexically ("10" before "2"); all 1,468 rows of SCF 2026.1.1 are plain integers 0-10, and a future release with a blank or non-numeric cell fails that one row loudly as a RenderError (recorded as a per-row "render() failed" error in src/generation/generation-engine.ts, not an aborted import) rather than silently scoring it 0 - which is what optional plus number would do, since Number('') is 0. curie is emitted automatically from the ontology plus the filename stem, so the recipe does not declare it. BODY, in order: the normative control description, the control question, SCR-CMM levels 1-5, and the five Possible Solutions and Considerations columns by organization size. No body heading repeats the note's own SCF # - Obsidian already renders the filename as the title. PROPERTIES VS BODY RATIONALE: the control description previously sat in a managed `description` property. At 173 characters average and 867 maximum it is unreadable in Obsidian's property panel, awkward to escape in YAML, and invisible to body search, so it is now the first body section. The SCR-CMM criteria (up to 2,407 characters each) and the solution lists have the same problem more acutely and were never emitted at all. MIGRATION: `description` is no longer a declared managed key, and computeManagedKeys in src/generation/frontmatter-merge.ts only manages keys the recipe currently declares, so a vault generated by the previous version of this recipe keeps a stale `description` property on re-import. Delete it once, or add it to user_preserve if you want to keep it. RIGHTS: RESTRICTED. The Secure Controls Framework workbook is CC BY-ND with separate derivative rules, so the source stays local-only under the fail-closed Frameworks/ gitignore. This recipe is a method - column mappings and literal headings, no framework prose - and is therefore publishable; generated SCF notes, sample output, and screenshots of SCF content are not. Corpus provenance and rights posture: https://cybersader.github.io/crosswalker/reference/framework-corpus/. DELIBERATE DROPS: (1) SCR-CMM Level 0 has only 2 distinct values across all 1,468 rows - it is the maturity model's fixed "not performed" definition and carries no per-control information, so 1,468 copies of it would be noise. (2) The three SCRM Focus tier columns are single-character "x" presence markers; the closed filter set has no boolean or presence filter (src/render/template.ts FILTERS), so they would emit as a literal "x" or an empty string, which is worse than omitting them. (3) "Errata 2026.1" cannot be addressed at all: resolvePath in src/render/template.ts:86 splits every template variable path on "." unconditionally with no escape, so any header containing a dot is unreachable. That is a second, smaller grammar gap worth recording. KNOWN GAP - relationship columns are intentionally not emitted. SCF's are: 250 authoritative-source mapping columns (NIST 800-53 R5, ISO 27002, CIS CSC 8.1 and the rest; 250 is the row count of the workbook's "Authoritative Sources" sheet), "Evidence Request List (ERL) #", "Risk Threat Summary" plus 39 per-risk columns, and "Control Threat Summary" plus 41 per-threat columns. All are newline-delimited identifier lists. managed_links can mechanically split such a cell (splitLinkValues in src/render/index.ts trims each piece and drops empties), but it can only wrap each piece in [[...]]: it cannot map an item to a CURIE, so Tier 2 closure could not traverse the result, and no bundled recipe creates the Evidence Request List, risk, or threat notes the links would point at, so every link would be unresolved. The cross-framework mapping columns are crosswalk edges and belong in an SSSOM mapping set produced from SCF's STRM bundle, not in control-note frontmatter. Half-resolving link lists are worse than none; this waits on a portable per-item transform and a relationship projection.
